Apple has added new hardware identifiers for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other devices, some of which may be announced as early as tomorrow at the "Surprise and Shine" event. Details below.

Apple backend adds new product data

With less than 24 hours to go before Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event, Apple appears to be updating its backend systems for upcoming devices.

According to Aaron Perris on X, Apple has added nearly 40 new hardware identifiers to its backend, including 7 iPhone identifiers.

Notably, the new iPhone hardware identifiers outnumber the 6 models currently rumored for the iPhone 18 lineup by one. Current rumors indicate Apple will announce three iPhones tomorrow (iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra), with the remaining models (including iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone 18e) expected to launch early next year.

That said, the extra identifier could simply be a variant of one of the other six devices rather than a brand-new device.

Back to the identifier list, it also includes 9 Mac identifiers, 8 iPad identifiers, 9 Apple Watch identifiers, 1 Apple TV identifier, and 3 identifiers in the HomeAccessory category.

While most of the identifiers cannot yet be matched to specific devices, some align with products Apple is known to be developing and that may be announced as early as tomorrow.

These include Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, a brand-new Apple TV, the long-rumored smart home hub, iMac and MacBook Pro models with M6 chips, and a new iPad mini with OLED display, among others.

9to5Mac will be on the ground at Apple Park for live coverage, so stay tuned for our reporting before and after the "Surprise and Shine" event.

What's your best guess for some of the new device identifiers? Let us know in the comments.
